To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

FGFR1 is amplified in a subset of primary CRCs and their corresponding metastases, that FGFR1 mRNA is expressed in all investigated CRCs and that FGFR1 protein expression is associated with the FGFR1 gene amplification.
FGFR1 is amplified in 5% of CRCs and its expression is independent of the FGFR1 ampliﬁcation status and its mRNA expression.
FGFR1 amplifications occur in about 5% of CRCs, that FGFR1 protein expression is not correlated with the amplification status and that FGFR1 is likely to be a suitable drug target in CRC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of FGFR1 biology in CRC and the identification of FGFR1 as an interesting therapeutic target in CRC.
the development and evaluation of novel biomarkers for personalized cancer treatment and the development of novel therapeutic approaches.
the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for the treatment of colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FGFR1 is not a suitable target in the majority of CRC, but that it may be an interesting target for a subgroup of patients with FGFR1 protein expression.
the FGFR1 status should be assessed in CRC tissue samples prior to FGFR1 inhibitor application in clinical trials.
FGFR1 is not a predictive marker for the efficacy of FGFGFR inhibitors in CRC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FGFR1 is not an appropriate target in the majority of CRC patients.
FGFR1 is not a suitable biomarker in colorectal cancer.
FGFR1 is not a suitable target for therapy of CRC, but that the FGFR1 protein might serve as a predictive biomark for FGFR inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FGFR1 protein expression is a better predictor of FGFR inhibitor response than the FGFR1 gene copy number.
FGFR1 protein expression is likely to represent the most suitable biomarker for patient stratification in future clinical trials with FGFR inhibitors.
FGFR1 amplifications and expression are rare events in CRC and that the FGFR1 expression status does not correlate with FGFR1 amplifcation.
